copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Norway and Senegal together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Senegal side, by +13.5pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Norway 1760 vs Senegal 1790: 30 points in favour of Senegal, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Senegal to win at 39%. The away side reads 39% on this distribution — the model's central case for Senegal.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 48%, the draw at 25%, and Senegal to win at 26%. Polymarket has Senegal at 26%, which prices out at American odds of +292; the model has the same side at 39%. The +13.5pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Senegal side that lower bound is 32% — +6.3pp clear of the market's 26%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Senegal side.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 32 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Senegal a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +13.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +13.5pp gap across model and market on the Senegal side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Senegal at 39%; Polymarket sits at 26%.
copy.title: Norway v Senegal · the model leans Senegal
